newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Americel to place 112.5 mln reais commercial paper.
newsitem.headline: Americel to place 112.5 mln reais commercial paper.

text.p: Americel S.A., a Canadian-led group that earlier this month won Brazil's first B Band cellular concession, will place 112.5 million reais in commercial papers, the bank coordinating the deal said.

Banco do Brasil said in a statement published in local newspapers that the firm will offer 225 Commercial Promissory Notes, each with a nominal value of 500,000 reais, beginning Monday in local markets.
The 30- to 180-day papers will be subscribed at face value with a discount to be applied on the payment date to reflect market conditions at the time of placement.
Americel, led by BCE Inc unit Bell Canada and Telesystem, also of Canada, was the lone bidder for a B Band concession area 7 covering central and western Brazil, including the capital of Brasilia.
The group, which also includes Citibank, local bank Opportunity and pension funds owned by Banco do Brasil, offered of 338.5 million reais, some 25.4 percent above the base price.
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso formally granted the concession on June 11, making it the first group to win one of Brazil's 10 B Band licenses.
Area 7 comprises the largely rural states of Acre, Goias, Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul, Rondonia and Tocantins states and the federal district of Brasilia.
Eight of nine other B Band concessions across the country are slated to be granted in the coming weeks.
Still to come are the coveted areas of Sao Paulo city and state, Rio de Janeiro and Espirito Santo states and Minas Gerais state, hotly contested areas where experts predict large premiums.
